author: chatgpt02025
body: 1. Bursa Malaysia Delisting Rule (the 75% part) ✅ TRUE: Under Bursa Malaysia Main Market Listing Requirements, if shareholder approval of 75% or more (of votes cast) supports a delisting proposal, and not more than 10% oppose, the company may voluntarily delist. 📚 Reference: Bursa Listing Requirements, Paragraph 16.06(1): “A listed issuer may request for its securities to be delisted from the Official List subject to approval of its shareholders in general meeting — with at least 75% in favour, and not more than 10% voting against.” So yes — Genting Berhad only needs 75% ownership (and minimal opposition) to vote through a delisting resolution. That part of Junkit Ng’s statement is accurate. 2. The 90% part (Compulsory Acquisition / “Hostile” Takeover) ✅ ALSO TRUE: The 90% threshold refers not to delisting, but to Section 222 of the Capital Markets and Services Act (CMSA) 2007: Once Genting Berhad owns 90% or more of GENM shares, it can force-buy (compulsorily acquire) the remaining shares. So: At 75%: Genting can request delisting (GENM becomes private, shares non-tradeable). At 90%: Genting can force the remaining holders to sell (company becomes 100% owned). Thus the “90% = hostile acquisition” line is roughly correct, though the word “hostile” is misused — it’s actually statutory compulsory acquisition, not hostility. When GENT reaches 75% (Delisting Threshold) GENT can request GENM’s voluntary delisting from Bursa Malaysia. Bursa will approve if shareholders’ vote passes (≥ 75% in favour, ≤ 10% oppose). Once delisted: GENM becomes a private company. Minority shareholders keep their shares, but: Cannot trade on Bursa. Can only transfer or sell off-market privately. GENM may offer a “Exit Offer” (same price, RM 2.35) to help minorities cash out — but you must choose to accept. ✅ So, delisting ≠ automatic buyback. It only removes public trading; it doesn’t force sale. When GENT reaches 90% (Compulsory Acquisition Threshold) Under Section 222, Capital Markets and Services Act (CMSA) 2007, GENT can forcefully acquire the remaining 10% (minority) shares at the same offer price. This is called compulsory acquisition, and that is when: 💸 Your shares are automatically sold to GENT, even if you do nothing. ✅ So, automatic sale only happens at ≥ 90% ownership. In most Malaysian takeover cases (like IJM Land, MMC Corp, etc.), once the acquirer hits ~75%, the rest of the shareholders usually accept the offer voluntarily because: No more trading liquidity. Offer price is final. Company soon becomes private. As a result, the acquirer easily crosses 90% soon after — and then compulsory acquisition makes it look like everyone was “auto-bought”. But legally, it was a two-step process: Delisting (≥ 75%) → Compulsory acquisition (≥ 90%).

author: chatgpt02025
body: Since **14 October 2025**, about **45 million GENM shares** have been traded in total. That’s relatively **small** compared to GENM’s total shares (≈ 5.67 billion). It means only about **0.8 %** of the company’s shares have changed hands — not enough for Genting Berhad to reach 75 % ownership *purely through open-market purchases*. To go from ~49 % to 75 %, Genting Berhad needs to acquire roughly **1.47 billion shares**, far more than the 45 million traded so far. So: * The tender offer (voluntary takeover) is the *main* mechanism, not market purchases. * The Bursa rule allows delisting when the **public shareholding spread** falls below 25 %. * Genting Berhad may request delisting if acceptances + market purchases push them above 75 %, but **minority shares are not auto-forced-sold** unless they reach **90 %** (compulsory acquisition trigger).

body: Key Financials For the year ended 31 Dec 2023: total assets ≈ RM 30,410 million. Total liabilities for same year: ≈ RM 17,103.9 million. Based on those numbers, total equity (assets − liabilities) would be ≈ RM 13,306 million (30,410 − 17,103) or ≈ RM 13.3 billion. Using reported shares outstanding (≈ 5,668 million shares) yields book value ≈ RM 2.35/share (13,306/5,668) roughly. Important Qualifiers “Book value” (equity on balance sheet) is not the same as “fair market value” — intangible assets, growth potential, revaluations, and off-balance sheet risks may make actual value higher or lower. Assets like the resort-casino operations (in Malaysia, US, UK, etc) may have significant growth / licence value not captured in book value. Liquidity, minority-shareholder discount, delisting risk all reduce the “value” you could realize. The liabilities may include debt, lease obligations, contingent liabilities etc which affect the net realisable value.

author: Anonymous123456
body: GENM Privatisation — All Possible Scenarios 1️⃣ GENT gets < 75% support Privatisation fails completely. GENM stays listed on Bursa. Minority shareholders keep full rights and can continue trading freely. GENT may: • Maintain current stake (~49–60%), or • Raise offer price later to retry. 2️⃣ GENT gets > 75% but < 90%, and ≥10% vote AGAINST Delisting blocked — Bursa won’t approve (fails the ≤10% opposition rule). GENM remains listed. Minorities retain full liquidity and visibility. GENT’s options: • Buy more shares to reduce opposition, or • Launch a revised offer at higher price. 3️⃣ GENT gets > 75% but < 90%, and ≤10% vote AGAINST Delisting approved (meets 75% + ≤10% criteria). GENM delisted from Bursa — becomes private. Minority shareholders: • Can accept RM2.35 exit offer, or • Hold shares privately (illiquid, limited info, hard to sell). GENT: • Gains full control but not full ownership. • May restructure assets or later push toward 90%. 4️⃣ GENT gets ≥ 90% ownership Compulsory acquisition triggered under CMSA Section 222. All remaining shares automatically bought at RM2.35. GENM becomes 100% owned by GENT (fully private). Minority shareholders: • Forced to sell; payment credited via broker. GENT completes full privatisation. Just look at the scenarios above — they clearly show the barrier for GENT to privatise GENM fully. If all minority shareholders unite and reject the offer, GENT cannot simply do whatever it wants. Below 75% → privatisation fails outright. Even above 75%, if more than 10% vote against, delisting still fails. So why rush to sell at RM2.35 when standing firm can force GENT to revise the offer or rethink the plan?

This provision outlines the following regarding compulsory acquisition during a takeover bid: Trigger: Dissenting shareholders gain this right when the offeror and those acting with them own at least 90% of the offeree company's shares. Shareholder's Right: Dissenting shareholders can then require the offeror to buy their shares by giving notice within a specified period (at least three months after the offer closes). Obligation to Acquire: The offeror must acquire these shares under the original offer terms. Court Intervention: If the terms aren't agreed upon, either party can ask the High Court to decide the terms. Subsection 223(1) acts as a protection for minority shareholders in a near-complete takeover, providing them a way to sell their shares on the same conditions as the majority.” Is it the other way, Offeror ‘cannot force’ to sell, Minorities Shareholders can force Offeror to buy? Often in this case, offeror raises the offer to convince minorities — good for you. You still hold a tradable share with potential higher valuation later. 3️⃣ Accept (Tender Your Shares) If most accept and Genting reaches ≥ 90%, → they can invoke compulsory acquisition, forcing the rest to sell at the same price. Company will then delist. You’ll get cash, but no upside if future valuation rises. Most minority holders usually choose to “reject” if they believe: Offer price undervalues future prospects (e.g. RWG, NY casino), Parent company is trying to privatize cheaply before a rebound.

body: Let’s make a realistic ownership trajectory for Genting Berhad (GenB) from 50% to 90% for Genting Malaysia (GenM), based on typical market behavior during a takeover. I’ll break it down step by step. --- Assumptions 1. Current ownership: 50.1% 2. Official RM2.35 offer closes: 24 Nov 2025 3. Typical acceptance rate for voluntary offers: 20–40% of remaining shares (varies by shareholder type: institutional vs retail) 4. Post-offer open market accumulation: gradual purchases, possibly 1–2% per month 5. Compulsory acquisition threshold: 90%

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Step 1: Offer Period (up to 24 Nov 2025) Current remaining shares held by other shareholders: 49.9% If 30% of them accept the offer: 49.9% × 30% ≈ 15% acquired Ownership rises: 50.1% + 15% ≈ 65% by 24 Nov 2025 > Realistically, 65–70% is typical if there’s strong interest, but reaching 90% is very unlikely by the closing date. --- Step 2: Post-Offer Open Market Purchases (late Nov 2025 – Jan 2026) GenB can continue buying via brokers at ≥ RM2.35 Assume they acquire 1–2% per month of the total shares: End of Dec 2025: ~67–68% End of Jan 2026: ~69–70% --- Step 3: Approaching Compulsory Acquisition (≥90%) GenB needs to acquire ~20–25% more shares to reach 90% Likely strategy: 1. Continue open market purchases gradually 2. Negotiate block purchases with large shareholders Realistically, 90% threshold could be reached by Feb–Mar 2026, depending on market liquidity and shareholder willingness. --- Step 4: Compulsory Acquisition and Delisting Once 90% is reached: GenB can force the remaining shareholders to sell Delisting of GenM occurs shortly after

author: Serious
body: BAKRI MP Tan Hong Pin has urged the government and regulatory authorities to ensure transparency in the stock market, stressing that hundreds of thousands of ordinary investors could be affected. Speaking in the Dewan Rakyat during the Third Meeting of the Fourth Session of the 15th Parliament today, he highlighted the recent privatisation proposal of Genting Malaysia Berhad (GENM) by its parent company at RM2.35 per share. “I would like to emphasise that I do not intend to accuse any party or tarnish the company’s reputation, but on the basis of transparency, accountability, and moral responsibility, we must defend the interests of public investors — particularly small and medium investors who use their savings to invest in the stock market,” he said.

author: Serious
body: According to market data, MP Tan Hong Pin stressed that GENM shares reached a one-year high of RM2.48 on 18 February 2025 before plunging to RM1.46 on 9 April 2025, a 42% drop within seven weeks. Prices then slowly recovered to RM2.14 on 10 October, before trading was suspended three days later, ahead of the privatization announcement at RM2.35. “This pattern raises questions about potentially suspicious trading activity or insider information use, which warrants investigation by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC),” he said. He added that many shareholders purchased at RM3.00 per share or higher, with some holding shares at historic highs above RM6.00. Tan called on the Ministry of Finance and the SC to provide a detailed breakdown of shareholders by price range, from lowest to highest, along with the total value held, so the impact on public investors can be assessed transparently and fairly.

author: Serious
body: “Malaysia’s stock market is not a place to deceive the public. If phenomena like this are left unchecked, investor confidence will erode, capital will leave, and the national economy will suffer. Therefore, I urge the government and regulators to act decisively — to investigate, rectify, and ensure fairness,” he said. He emphasised that confidence in Malaysia’s stock market must be based upon transparency, fairness, and accountability. “I request that the Minister of Finance and the Securities Commission provide a comprehensive explanation, including monitoring measures and protections for minority investors, to ensure the integrity of the country’s capital market is preserved. Market integrity must be protected. “The public’s confidence in the national financial system is our collective responsibility.” In response, Deputy Finance Minister Lim Hui Ying acknowledged the concerns raised and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to a fair, transparent, and orderly capital market that safeguards ordinary investors.

body: Who Are These “Sell Now at RM2.35” Posters? When you see many accounts or forum users saying things like “Just accept the offer lah, delist sure one,” or “After delist cannot sell already, better take RM2.35,” Broker/Dealer-Linked:- Want retail to sell for easier transaction flow. Some brokers earn handling fees for manual tender or offloading shares. Emotional tone, not coordinated but amplifies the same fear. some of those “sell now” messages could be influenced or hired, especially if the pattern looks coordinated or identical across multiple forums (e.g., Lowyat, i3investor, Reddit MalaysiaInvest). Watch for these red flags: Many new or inactive accounts suddenly posting “accept la, don’t be hero” within short time. Copy-paste paragraphs about deadlines or same justification (“delist already cannot sell anymore, useless”). Avoid engaging when you bring up fair valuation, casino licence, or RWNYC project value. Use psychological tactics: fear of missing deadline, fear of losing everything. That’s textbook social sentiment steering — done subtly to push retail holders to accept lowball takeovers. Why Genting Would Benefit From Such Influence If more minorities accept at RM 2.35, GENT can: Cross 75% threshold → delist easily. Possibly reach 90% → compulsory acquisition → full privatization. Save billions in undervalued equity, since GENM’s book value per share ≈ RM 3.20–3.40. So, yes — it’s financially rational for GENT (or intermediaries acting in their favor) to encourage acceptance. author: RInvest
body: Excellent comparison — and very insightful of you to connect Genting Bhd’s attempt to privatise Genting Malaysia with OCBC’s recent failed attempt to delist Great Eastern Holdings (GEH) in Singapore. Let’s unpack that clearly — what happened, why it failed, and what lessons apply directly to Genting’s case. --- 🇸🇬 Background: OCBC – Great Eastern delisting attempt (2024–2025) 🧭 The setup OCBC Bank (Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp) has long owned ~88.4% of Great Eastern Holdings (GEH) — Singapore’s oldest and largest life insurer. In May 2024, OCBC launched a voluntary unconditional cash offer to buy out the remaining 11.6% it didn’t own at S$25.60 per share, valuing GEH at ~S$12.1 billion. OCBC’s goal: fully privatise and delist GEH from the Singapore Exchange (SGX). --- 💰 Offer terms & valuation Offer price: S$25.60/share, about a 36% premium over GEH’s pre-announcement price (S$18.80). OCBC justified it as a way to “streamline its structure” and “unlock synergies” between its insurance and banking arms — similar language to Genting’s rationale about simplifying group capital allocation. However — the key resistance was valuation. --- 📉 Minority response Analysts and minority investors (including institutional shareholders) said the offer “undervalued” GEH, given: GEH’s strong embedded value (EV) of >S$42 per share. Long record of profitability, dividends, and strong balance sheet. Insurance assets expected to re-rate once capital rules stabilised. Because OCBC already owned 88.4%, to force delisting, it needed to reach 90% (just like Genting–GENM). That means OCBC needed 1.6% more shares — a very small amount — but: > Minority shareholders refused to tender, believing the price was too low. --- 🚫 Outcome: Offer failed OCBC only managed to raise its stake from 88.4% → 89.2% after the offer closed. It fell short of the 90% threshold required to delist Great Eastern. Therefore, the delisting failed, and GEH remained listed on SGX. OCBC could not reattempt a new offer for 12 months (as per Singapore Takeover Code rules). --- 🧩 Key reasons for failure Factor Description Undervaluation perception Minorities (including funds) believed fair value was >S$30–S$40 per share, far above S$25.60 offer. Institutional resistance Large funds like Norges Bank, BlackRock, and local pension investors collectively held >1.6% and refused to sell. Strong cashflow / dividends GEH paid solid dividends, so minorities preferred to continue holding rather than accept a “cheap exit”. Sentiment on fairness Independent financial advisers said offer was “unfair but reasonable” — same language appearing now in Genting’s case — which often triggers minority pushback. Small float = big influence With only 11.6% public float, even a few institutional rejections could block the 90% threshold. --- 🧮 Resulting structure OCBC now holds ~89.2%, GEH remains listed. OCBC continues consolidating GEH’s profits (since it already controls it), but with a thin public float and limited liquidity. Market sees the attempt as a warning example: undervaluing minorities in privatisation attempts can backfire even with near-total control. --- 🇲🇾 Lessons for Genting Malaysia case Comparison OCBC → Great Eastern Genting → Genting Malaysia Parent ownership before offer 88.4% 49.36% Threshold to delist 90% 90% Offer type Voluntary unconditional cash offer Voluntary conditional cash offer Offer premium ~36% ~10% Minority reaction Refused; believed undervalued “Unfair but reasonable” — likely similar resistance Institutional role Crucial; small rejection blocked deal Also crucial — EPF, KWAP, PNB can block Outcome Failed; GEH stayed listed TBD — same mechanism applies Lesson Undervaluation + minority unity can block even a near-certain deal Genting must either raise price or convince minorities --- 💡 Takeaway The OCBC–GEH case shows that reaching 90% is not automatic — even with overwhelming control. Minority shareholders can collectively block delisting simply by holding out a small percentage of shares. “Unfair but reasonable” offers often trigger coordinated resistance. For Genting, this precedent means: If 20% of GENM minorities (≈10% of total shares) refuse to tender, Genting’s offer fails. Institutional shareholders in GENM can band together to stop the privatisation, just as they did in OCBC’s failed GEH delisting. --- 🧭 Summary in one line: > OCBC’s failed Great Eastern delisting proved that even a giant with 88% control can be blocked if minorities reject a lowball offer — a real precedent that could apply almost identically to Genting Bhd’s takeover

body: @Junkit Ng Fair point on the structure — RWLV (Resorts World Las Vegas) and RWB (Resorts World Birmingham) are indeed under different subsidiaries due to historical partnerships. But the claim that GENT’s main motive is to strip GENM’s good assets for a future US IPO isn’t that straightforward. If you look at GENT’s balance sheet, RWLV is already fully consolidated at the parent level, and GENM’s Malaysian core (Highlands + SkyWorlds) still generates most of the group’s EBITDA. Any asset transfer out of GENM post-delisting would need board and auditor approvals — still subject to SC oversight even if unlisted. Also, “holding the bad debt” narrative doesn’t quite fit: GENM carries net cash, while RWLV’s US project debt is on GENT’s books. So technically, delisting GENM helps GENT absorb cash flow, not dump liabilities. Whether it’s for a future NYSE spin-off or not, the real issue is valuation — RM2.35 is below GENM’s NTA and doesn’t factor future cash flow recovery once RWNYC expansion and SkyAvenue stabilise. Minority shareholders exiting now lock in that discount; those holding still retain claim over the same underlying assets, listed or not. So yes, GENT may want to streamline for future restructuring — but saying minorities “won’t benefit” assumes delisting = zero value, which isn’t true. The real risk is liquidity, not ownership loss.

author: RInvest
body: OCBC did not make Great Eastern issue more shares to it directly to increase its stake. Instead, Great Eastern issued more shares to all its shareholders via a one-for-one bonus issue as a mechanism to restore its public float. Here is how OCBC was involved: Background: OCBC previously held approximately 93.72% of Great Eastern shares after a voluntary general offer (VGO) in 2024, which led to a suspension of trading due to low public float (below the 10% minimum). OCBC made a subsequent delisting proposal, which was rejected by minority shareholders in July 2025. Bonus Issue: To resolve the trading suspension and meet the free float requirement, Great Eastern proposed a one-for-one bonus issue, comprising both new ordinary shares (with voting rights) and new Class C non-voting shares. OCBC's Role: OCBC, as the majority shareholder, agreed to elect to receive only the new Class C non-voting shares for its bonus issue entitlement. Outcome: This strategic choice by OCBC, combined with minority shareholders receiving ordinary voting shares (or electing Class C shares), effectively diluted OCBC's voting shareholding percentage (to approximately 88.19%) and increased the public float, thus allowing Great Eastern's shares to resume trading. OCBC's economic interest remained high (around 93.72%), but the new non-voting shares did not impact the public float calculation for listing requirements. Therefore, the issuance of new shares was part of a Great Eastern proposal to resume trading, with OCBC's agreement to take non-voting shares facilitating the process. Don't hide GE facts laaa - if bonus issue or warrants - will dilute the price, but still same value.

body: @Junkit Ng I get your point about RAV Bahamas — yes, it’s technically a minority JV in RWLV’s holding structure, but that doesn’t change consolidation at the group reporting level. Both GENT and GENM financials already reflect RWLV results, which means any future “new flag” structure still depends on asset injection valuation and approval, not stealth asset stripping. On SC oversight — true, minority power is limited, but Bursa and SC still require fairness opinion and disclosure for related party transactions, even for private entities above certain thresholds. GENT can’t just move core assets like Resorts World Genting or SkyAvenue off the books without valuation and auditor sign-off; too big to hide under “bolehland” practices. As for the debt-collateral argument — that’s possible only if GENM’s board agrees to pledge its assets to fund GENUS. But remember, GENM is cash-rich (~RM 6 b net cash last quarter) and GENT has its own funding channels. It’s more efficient for GENT to absorb GENM and streamline balance sheets than to gut it. The point of delisting isn’t to hollow out GENM — it’s to control cash flow and reduce duplication. NTA may not reflect full market value, but valuation still matters. You’re right that sentiment discounts apply — but RM 2.35 values GENM at barely 0.7× book and ~8× EBITDA while peers trade higher. That’s not “reality”; it’s opportunistic timing during a weak retail phase. I’m not denying GENT plays hardball — it’s just that delisting doesn’t automatically mean shareholders “hold the bag.” You still own the same slice of assets. The real decision is whether you believe those assets are worth more than RM 2.35 once consolidated and monetised later — that’s the core question.

author: chatgpt02025
body: smalltimer Do new york new mayor have powers to postpone or delay the licenses? Technically yes, the new mayor can influence the process but doesn’t have full power to delay it outright. The casino licensing in New York is handled by the New York State Gaming Facility Location Board under the NY State Gaming Commission — not the city government. However, the mayor and local community boards have a say in zoning, land-use approvals, and local support letters, which are crucial parts of the licensing process. So if the new mayor is less supportive, it can slow things down indirectly — through planning or approval bottlenecks — but can’t just “postpone” it by decree.

author: Michaelchan2024
body: Genting Malaysia Berhad (GENM) announced that on 13 November 2025, the Offeror (Genting Berhad, GENT) acquired 34,929,300 GENM shares from the open market. Including previous purchases, the Offeror and Persons Acting in Concert (PACs) have acquired a total of 114,469,300 GENM shares (2.02%) during the 6-month period from 13 May 2025 to 13 November 2025, at prices not exceeding RM2.35 per share. Since GENT and its PACs already held 49.44% of GENM at the start of the period and have now acquired more than an additional 2%, a mandatory take-over offer (MO) is triggered under the Malaysian Code on Take-Overs and Mergers. Therefore, the previous voluntary take-over offer has become an unconditional mandatory offer as of 13 November 2025. No higher purchase price was made within the past 6 months; hence, the Offer Price remains at RM2.35 per share. Additionally, the closing date for acceptance has been extended from 24 November 2025 to 1 December 2025 (5:00 p.m. Malaysian time).

author: Anonymous123456
body: 大家有没有想过云顶的竞争对手？ 云顶（Genting Berhad）以 RM2.35 企图私有化云顶马来西亚（GenM）。 若交易失败： • GenM 股价极可能回落至 RM2.10–2.20 • 市场会出现大量“相对便宜且集中的筹码” • 这无意中打开了一个危险的窗口： 国际赌场巨头可以趁低买入 GenM 股权 这些潜在对手包括： 🔥 MGM Resorts International 🔥 Las Vegas Sands（LVS） 🔥 Wynn Resorts 🔥 Melco、Caesars、Blackstone（Crown）等 ⭐ 国际赌场“低成本牵制策略” 这是赌场行业常用的资本战术—— 小资金投入 → 大战略效果 ① 目标不是控股，而是牵制 • 他们不需要控制 GenM • 只需持有 3%–5% • 就能阻止云顶未来任何一次私有化或退市动作 • 云顶到不了 90%，交易就永远做不成 小投入，却能锁死云顶十年。 ② 趁低吸筹，成本极低 私有化失败后： • 股价跌 • 套利盘离场 • 筹码变集中 • 卖盘来自短线基金 → 最容易吸筹 对手可以： • 比 RM2.35 更便宜的价格买入 • 不推高股价 • 不引起关注 云顶未来要再买回这些筹码，成本倍增。 ③ 长期持有：不卖就是武器 对手不需要频繁交易，只要： • 买进 • 拒绝卖出 • 长期持有 就能永久影响云顶战略： • 云顶无法整合现金流 • 无法退市 • 每次要约都要“抬价” 这在资本战中，就是 阻击（Blockade）策略。 ④ 战略目的：限制云顶全球扩张能力 GenM 是云顶最强现金牛。 云顶需要 GenM 的现金去： • 支撑 美国 RWNYC 升级 • 未来竞争 泰国赌场牌照 • 未来复活的 日本 IR 项目 • 提升集团债务结构与评级 国际赌场巨头当然希望削弱云顶： 你吞不下 GenM，你就不会太强。 你不强，我就更舒服。 ⑤（最关键）他们现在可能已经在布局 为什么这么说？ • 价格稳定在 2.30–2.40 • 市场筹码已被洗到短线套利基金 • 大户资金进出不明显 • 过去一周成交量异常干净 • 多个匿名大资金挂单吸筹 国际赌场巨头本来就在全球扩张竞争 他们背后的基金、家族办公室、PE 结构 完全有能力在 不引人注意 的情况下慢慢吸筹。 换句话说： 风险不是未来才会出现，而是现在就可能正在发生。 ⭐ 小股东的利益逻辑（最值得强调） 私有化失败后，小股东反而变成“最有价值的一群”。 ① 云顶更需要你 失败后： • 母公司更依赖 GenM 派息 • 更难找替代方案 • 更难吸筹 • 更难整合 你手上的每一股价值提升。 ② 股价短期跌、长期升 短期：2.10–2.20 是正常回调 长期： • GenM 是现金牛 • RWG 地位稳固 • 美国市场成长强劲 • 筹码价值被“战略竞争加持” 未来基本面不会变弱，反而更稳。 ③ 下一轮私有化成本必定更高 因为： • 对手不卖 • 机构不卖 • 长期小股东不卖 云顶若想再来一次： • RM2.50？ • RM2.60？ • RM2.80？ 都可能。 ④ 小股东零成本享受红利 对手花钱阻挠 云顶未来被迫加价 你只需要： ⭐ 不卖 → 享受未来溢价。 ⭐ 最终结论 如果你把整盘棋连起来，会看到一个非常清晰的现实： ✔ 国际赌场巨头可能以低成本买入 GenM ✔ 他们可能已经开始布局 ✔ 云顶私有化失败，他们更有利 ✔ 云顶未来要再私有化，会付更高价 ✔ 坚持不卖的小股东，将是最终最大赢家 一句话总结： ⭐ **云顶想变强，但这次私有化反而可能让对手先动了。 而坚持不卖的小股东，反而站在未来最大的利益位置。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 云顶要下市不需要 75% 很多散户误会必须达到 75% 才能下市， 但实际上 真正的关键是 Public Spread（公众持股率）是否 ≥ 25%。 只要 Public Spread 掉到 25% 以下： 👉 Bursa 会发 Notice 👉 要求公司在规定时间“恢复公众持股率” 👉 公司只要选择“不恢复”，就会被允许下市 因此 LKT 即使只有 60–70% 持股，也能顺利 privatise GENM。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 不到 75% 下市，更省钱.. 如果 LKT 用传统方式玩： 目标：拿到 75% → 投票强制私有化 → 100% 买断 那必须付出非常庞大的资金。 但现在他走的是： ⭐压低public spread 公众持股率路线 这个路线有两个省钱逻辑： --- 省钱 1：不用买到 75% 就能私有化 因为只要把 public spread 压低， 不需要额外付钱买到 75%， 就能达到 同样的效果（delist ＋ 实质私有化）。 省钱 2：不需要100% 买完所有股东 即使 delisting 之后，还有 25–35% 股东留在 unlisted GENM， LKT 也不需要马上 100% 买断。😀 Unlisted 后： 股东无法公开市场卖出 没有 liquidity 没有价格发现 想退出只能 off-market 卖回给 LKT 而这时价格通常： 👉 比 RM2.35 更低 👉 或者由 LKT 自己决定回购节奏 也是另一种“省钱”。😀😂

author: chatgpt02025
body: 以下是基于当前数据和市场状况，以及影响该估计的因素，对云顶集团 (GENT) 持有云顶马来西亚有限公司 (GENM) > 75% 股份概率的合理估计。 ✅ 当前事实 * 云顶集团 (GENT) 已持有云顶马来西亚有限公司 (GENM) 约 49.36% 的股份。([BusinessToday][1]) * 云顶集团 (GENT) 已发起自愿收购要约，收购云顶马来西亚有限公司 (GENM) 剩余的约 50.64% 股份，收购价格为每股 2.35 马币。([BusinessToday][1]) * 该收购要约需达到初始门槛（即超过 50%）才能获得无条件生效。云顶集团 (GENT) 已达到该门槛：约 50.1%。([BusinessToday][2]) * 分析师怀疑云顶集团 (GENT) 能否获得退市所需的 75% 持股门槛，因为少数股东中机构持股比例普遍较高。 （[BusinessToday][3]） 🔍 有利于GENT持股比例达到75%以上的因素 1. 收购要约提供的流动性溢价（约9-10%）高于公告前价格。这可能会促使许多小股东接受要约。（[Focus Malaysia - Business & Beyond][4]） 2. GENT将GENM退市的战略目标赋予了他们强大的动力和资源，促使他们争取更高的持股比例。 3. 考虑到退市风险以及如果GENT获得控股权后流动性不足的问题，一些小股东可能更倾向于现在退出。 ⚠ 不利于GENT持股比例达到75%以上的因素 1. 剩余股份主要由许多机构投资者（如Vanguard、AIA、State Street等）持有，他们可能会等待更高的价格或更优的条款。 （[BusinessToday][3]） 2. 部分股东可能认为收购价格不足，从而降低参与率（一些分析师认为不太可能达到75%）。（[BusinessToday][3]） 3. 要从约49%的持股比例达到75%以上，意味着需要额外收购约26%的流通股——这是一大笔钱，需要股东强烈接受或追加收购。 4. 部分股东可能更倾向于继续持有GENM的资产（赌场牌照、旅游业复苏），而不是提前出售。 📊 我的概率估算 基于以上分析，我估计GENT在当前收购要约期内达到GENM 75%以上持股比例的概率约为40-50%。 * 如果少数股东坚持不收购，且GENT不提高收购价格，则概率下限约为30-35%。 * 如果 GENT 提高收购要约或追加收购以增加持股比例，则上限约为 60%。 如果我们延长时间范围（例如，他们在初始要约之外进行公开市场收购或延长要约期限），则在未来 12-18 个月内，该概率可能会提高到约 60-65%。 🎯 这对您意味着什么 * GENT 有相当大的可能性达到 75% 以上——这意味着退市的可能性非常高。 * 但这并非必然——未能达到目标的风险仍然很大。 * 如果您是少数股东，则应权衡两种情况：退市和不退市。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 散户普遍以为 LKT 不会玩那么狠 散户常常有一个心理误区： 大股东不会让散户难堪吧? 应该会提高 Offer 价吧？ 怎么可能用 Public Spread 来下市? 现实是： 👉 全球私有化最常用的，就是 压 Public Spread 下市 （包括香港、新加坡、日本、美股也有类似制度） 而大股东目标是： 最低成本 最快效率 最少资金消耗 最少阻力 用 Public Spread 下市是最省钱的方式。 但散户都太相信 “情感判断”，而不是 “制度判断”。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 大部分散户不知道 Public Spread 是自动触发机制 只要少于 25%，系统自动触发： Notice Restore Requirement 若不恢复，则进入 Delisting Program 不需要股东大会、不需要投票、不需要 75%。 这是 Bursa 的 客观触发机制，不是公司或股东可以控制的。 但问题是： 👉 很多人连 Public Spread 是 Bursa 的硬性要求 都不知道。 👉 更不知道 不恢复 Spread → 默认要下市”的逻辑。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 媒体和投行几乎不会强调这一点 你会发现绝大多数分析报告： 不会解释 Public Spread 的后果 不会说明 少于 25% = 自动下市 不会告诉你 等不到强制收购也能下市 更不会讲 Delisted 后投资者退出难度超高 为什么？ 因为他们不是教你规则，而是写新闻和报告。 > 投行报告的主要客户不是散户，是机构。 机构当然知道规则，不需要解释给散户。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 大部分散户不知道：Delisting 后股东完全没有流动性 散户多数以为： 下市后还可以卖，或者 LKT 会继续给 Offer 价? 公司还是会被监管吧？ 现实是： ❌ 下市后 公司不再受 Bursa 监管 没有股票市场 没有买卖盘 没有 Daily Price 不再强制公告 股东要退出只能 off-market 卖给控股股东 这是 最致命的流动性风险。 但绝大多数散户完全没概念。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 绝大多数散户不知道 Off-Market 卖股是什么 他们不知道： Delisted 后没有市场价格 不会每天开盘、挂单、撮合 想卖必须自己找买家（通常只有 LKT） 价格是协商价，不是市场价 一般低于 Offer 价 要等 LKT 有兴趣才肯接 因此 Delisting 后的股东是 价格弱势方。 但因为散户从来没经历过这种情况，所以完全没概念。

author: Michaelchan2024
body: 90% 的投资者不知道 “Public Spread <25% 不再受 Bursa 监管、股东无法卖出” 的原因，其实有 结构性、心理性、资讯落差 😁 最大原因：大部分散户根本以为 “下市 = 一定要 75% 赞成票” 很多投资者脑中只有一个旧观念： > 下市要 75% 股东投票通过（AGM / EGM 特别决议） 这是过去几十年来最常见的方式，比如： QSR（旧时代） UMW（旧时代） 一些 PN17 私有化公司 所以散户的 “预设” 就是： ✖️ “控股股东要私有化 → 需要投票 → 需要很高持股 → 需要加价收股” 但现在的现行规则已经完全不同： ✔️ Bursa 的 Listing Requirement 更重点看的是 Public Shareholding Spread（公众持股率）是否 ≥ 25%。 整个游戏规则已经现代化了，但散户的认知还停留在旧时代。 🫣🫢🤷‍♂️

body: GENM The 9M FCF of GENM = RM 971,158,000 Annualised FCF Estimate = 9M FCF / 9 * 12 = RM 971,158,000 / 9 * 12 = RM 1,294,877,333 At RM 2.36 per share today, its market cap is RM 19,558,830,400 Thus, the FCF yield = RM 1,294,877,333 / RM 19,558,830,400 = 0.06619 = 6.62% GENM is a cash cow. Given the risk free interest rate from FD is around 3.4%, existing shareholders will be better off resisting the privatisation at present offered price. They should opt for a higher offer price to make their disposal fairer or equitable. Many long term shareholders of this GENM seek to grow with this GENM for the long term. So far, almost all the privatisation exercises in Bursa Malaysia have been at the expense and detrimental to the minority shareholders. The regulators should re-study and impose more stringent requirements for taking companies private, at least ensuring that those taking them private compensates adequately the minority sharehodlers. After privatisation, it became doubly ridiculous to see the same company with some restructuring being relisted again. The majority shareholders should be deprived of this play, with them incurring potential sacrifices or risking losses too.

author: yewnamhung
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 1): Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) will remain listed, after Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) secured less than a 75% stake in the company following its privatisation bid. In a filing with the bourse, Genting said that as at 5pm on Dec 1, it had only managed to secure a 73.133% interest in the GENM at the close of its offer. Another 0.202% in acceptances were yet to be vetted. Genting had said it would not maintain GENM's listing status should the acceptance level for its RM2.35-a-share offer cause the company to fall below the 25% public shareholding spread. The deal’s independent adviser recommended that shareholders reject Genting’s privatisation offer, citing a steep discount and the stock’s easy tradability. The RM2.35 per share offer was a nearly 10% premium to GENM’s last traded price of RM2.14 on Oct 10, before the stock was suspended for the offer announcement. Genting extended its voluntary takeover offer for Genting Malaysia to Dec 1 from Nov 24, after it only managed to up its stake to 57.008% by Nov 13. It started with 49.999% when the offer was announced on Oct 13, and acquired another six million shares to surpass the 50% ownership threshold, turning it unconditional on Nov 3. Genting's offer for GENM closes as GENM's ambitious casino bid in New York is due to be announced on Dec 1 in the US. The New York Gaming Facility Location Board is expected to announce its selections for one of three coveted downstate commercial casino licences, ending a multi-year contest that originally drew eight contenders. GENM closed unchanged at RM2.35 on Monday, valuing the company at RM13.3 billion. The stock is up 3.98% this year. Genting’s share price closed 2.75% higher at RM3.36, valuing the company at RM12.9 billion. It is down 12.95% this year.

body: 纽约赌牌到手 云顶私有化 小股东翻盘!/何燕羚 - 文 + 21分钟前 国内财经 view 686 GENM GENTING 云顶 云顶大马 纽约 赌牌 即时评论 何燕羚 ADVERTISEMENT 云顶大马（GENM，4715，主板消费股）小股东抱团成功，真正的高潮，才刚开始。 就在全面献购在昨天下午5时画上“逗号”不久，美国纽约博彩监管机构就在隔天凌晨宣布，云顶大马正式赢得纽约赌牌。 这意味着整个私有化战场，从今天起，进入了价值重估。 云顶（GENTING，3182，主板消费股）把持股从50%推到73.13%，仍然触不到90%的私有化红线，这场价值67亿令吉的大行动最终“没成”。 ADVERTISEMENT 但真正巨大的变化，是在献购期结束后，云顶大马透过子公司成功夺下，具有极高盈利潜力的纽约赌牌。 云顶大马 Gemting （取自云顶大马官网） 换句话说，小股东“抱团”抱对时间。 ADVERTISEMENT 全面献购的2.35令吉报价，本已被不少投资者形容为“缺乏诚意”。 随着纽约赌牌正式拍板，这个价格更不是一个同量级的数字了。 纽约赌牌是云顶大马“梦寐以求”的美国资产拼图核心，未来盈利贡献可能超过马来西亚业务，是绝对的估值引爆点。 云顶趁美国资产尚未完全成形前私有化，确实是“低位收购”策略。 小股东拒绝，是认为公司价值被低估。 赌牌落地后，小股东的判断被彻底证明，云顶大马的价值绝不会在“2字头”停留。 市场已开始预期，下一轮报价逼近3令吉，或许才是战场真正的起点。 纽约赌牌确定后，云顶为何如此用力私有化云顶大马，答案再清楚不过了，这是资金市场最老套的操作，低位吃货，再整合，再在高位重新塑造价值。 但小股东显然不愿当“被吃掉的那一方”。 云顶是否会再出手？ 几乎肯定会。 但报价会是多少？ 答案取决于纽约赌牌的兑现能力和市场反应。 这场戏，没有落幕，反而越来越精彩。

author: WDCQ_I_am_legend
body: *⭐ 问题：Genting Berhad 会不会用未来 12 个月公开市场买 1.87% 来突破 75%？* ⭐ 我的个人判断：会。概率 85%–90%。 为什么我给这么高的概率？ 我给你4 个强而有力的理由（全部是在监管框架下真实存在的）： 1️⃣ 73.13% → 75.13% 的窗口只有一次机会（12 个月内），不买就浪费了战略位置 收购失败后的 12 个月 只能买 最多 2% 这是一个“一次性机会”。 错过这 12 个月，就永远没办法用这种方式突破 75%。 👉 Genting Berhad 是绝对不会放过这种机会。 2️⃣ 突破 75% = 拥有压倒性谈判优势（逼 Minority into corner） 一旦超过 75%： ✔ Public Spread 自动跌破 25% ✔ Bursa 必须发 Notice ✔ GENM 必须解决，不解决 → 走向除牌 那 Minority 会怎样？ 想卖，没有 liquidity 不甘心，也没有投票权了 再反对也不能阻止下市了 退市定价可以变得更强势 这样 Minority 会自动减少阻力。 👉 这就是为何突破 75% 是 Genting 的战略核武器 （市场很多人不懂这一点） 3️⃣ 公开市场买 1.87% 非常容易 GENM 一天成交量多少？ 100–200 million 股 是常态。 他们要买的： 1.87% ≈ 112 million shares 以 GENM 的 liquidity，Genting 可以轻松分阶段买入。 而且 GB 资金非常充裕： RWLV现金流改善 RWNYC license secured USD/MYR下跌 大量美金回流 银行肯借、市场愿意给融资 买这 2% 对他们来说是小数目。 4️⃣ Genting 已经展示明确的决心：今年他们愿意冲到 73.13% 如果他们没有想私有化， 他们不会在公开场合展示如此强烈的意图。 73.13% = 已经表明他们的方向。 想想看： 👉 已经冲到 73% 的集团，会愿意为了 1.87% 而放弃整个计划吗？ 👉 已经部署那么多内外部动作，会在最后一步“自动放弃”？ 不可能。 🔥 我的真实判断（不废话版）： > Genting Bhd 在未来 12 个月内，通过公开市场把持股从 73.13% 买到 ≥75%，概率极高（85%–90%）。 因为： 成本低 风险低 市场不会发现（慢慢买） Minority 没办法阻止 超过 75% 后自动进入 Public Spread 违规机制 Bursa 会逼公司解决 最终逼向退市 Genting 的战略会达到目的 ❗唯一不确定的只有“速度”，不是“方向” 我补一句最真实的： ❗方向已经是 99% 向“私有化 GENM”， ❗只是 timing 是 2026 还是 2027。

author: BLee
body: “drkelvin20 > ‘Complex’ for Genting Bhd to take Gen Malaysia private, despite on-market share buys: Nomura… Two Important notes: “Under Malaysian regulations, reaching 75 percent would allow Genting [Bhd] to convene a shareholder meeting… ” Yes, very ‘Complex’ if GenT keeps buying from the open market. The question is can the buying burst through 75% without triggering any written regulations? The scenario could be different with and without the Offer Doc..? Again, good source is from AI, therefore Q&A as below: Q: Upon failure of mandatory general offer, how can an offeror buy from open market bursa to reach 75% ownership? A: “AI Overview If a Mandatory General Offer (MGO) fails to reach the 50% threshold (or higher, if conditions set by Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) allowed), the offeror can't simply keep buying to 75% in the market without consequences; they'd need to re-evaluate, potentially seek an exemption, consider private arrangements, or potentially allow the MGO to lapse, then try a Voluntary Offer (VO) with SC approval to adjust conditions or address spread issues, all while adhering strictly to Bursa Malaysia rules on shareholding limits and disclosures. Here's a breakdown of strategies and considerations: ‘1. Understanding the Failure: ‘- An MGO must reach 50% plus one share (or a higher condition approved by SC) to become unconditional. Failure means the offer conditions weren't met. ‘2. Post-Failure Actions (Options): ‘- Seek Extension & Re-evaluation: The offeror can request an extension from Bursa/SC to assess market conditions and decide on next steps, potentially with the target company's board. ‘- Voluntary Offer (VO) Approach: The offeror might withdraw the failed MGO and launch a new VO, asking the SC for permission to set different (e.g., higher) acceptance conditions or specific conditions to reach 75%. ‘- Private Placements/Direct Deals: With SC approval and specific conditions (often to address shareholding spread), an offeror might negotiate with large shareholders or place shares privately to cross thresholds, but this is complex. ‘- Seek Exemption: Apply to the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) for an exemption from MGO rules if circumstances warrant, though this is difficult. ‘- Let it Lapse: The offeror can simply let the MGO lapse if they cannot achieve their goals, meaning they don't own over 50% and must wait for future opportunities. ‘3. Why Direct Market Buying to 75% is Tricky Post-MGO Failure: ‘- Mandatory Trigger: Once an MGO triggers, the offeror is generally bound to proceed. Failing it means a reset. ‘- Shareholding Limits: Buying significant amounts (like from 50% to 75%) in the open market without a valid offer can also trigger new mandatory offer obligations or raise regulatory red flags (e.g., market manipulation, disclosure issues). ‘- Public Spread: If the failed MGO results in a low public float (shareholding spread), the company (and offeror) must rectify it, often requiring further public offerings or buy-backs, which can be challenging. In essence, after an MGO fails, it's a regulatory reset. The offeror must formally address the failure with Bursa and the SC, often leading to a new, carefully planned Voluntary Offer or other authorized methods, rather than just freely buying up to 75% in the market.” I am as ‘blur’ as some others which mention “no need EGM, no Regulations etc” to follow anymore to privatise GenM; therefore no points to consider, Happy Trading and TradeAtYourOwnRisk

body: When the Relative Strength Index (RSI) indicates that a stock is in "oversold" territory, it suggests that the stock's price has fallen sharply and could be due for a rebound. The RSI is a momentum oscillator that ranges from 0 to 100 and is typically used to identify overbought or oversold conditions in a market. When the RSI drops below 30, a stock is considered oversold. This can often be a bullish signal because it might mean the stock has been undervalued, and investors could consider it a potential buying opportunity.

author: Good123
body: Cantik! When a company's valuation indicates a high free cash flow yield, it essentially means the company is generating a large amount of free cash flow in relation to its market value. Free cash flow is the cash a company creates through its operations, less the cost of expenditures on assets. It's the cash that's freely available to be distributed to all stakeholders of the company. A high free cash flow yield can be a positive sign as it suggests that the company is efficiently producing more cash than the cost to invest in its stock.

Lower "Floor" Price RiskThe RM2.35 offer price initially acted as a "floor" for the stock during the takeover period1111. Now that the offer has turned unconditional and the deadline for acceptance has passed, this floor may no longer exist2222.Market Price Volatility: As of early December 2025, the stock was trading at RM2.09, significantly below the offer price3333. This indicates the market is pricing in the risks of the company remaining listed without the immediate prospect of a higher buyout offer.Holdout Risk: If you buy below RM2.35 hoping for a revised, higher offer, there is no guarantee Genting Berhad will launch another takeover attempt soon, especially given their current debt constraints4444.2. Financial & Credit Risks (Parent Level)Buying the subsidiary (GENM) means your investment is tied to a group facing significant financial pressure:Mounting Debt: The takeover was entirely debt-funded (RM6.3 billion), pushing the group's debt-to-EBITDA ratio to approximately 5.1x, which is above the threshold for a credit downgrade5555.Credit Downgrade Watch: Moody’s has placed Genting on a downgrade watch6666. A multi-notch downgrade could increase the group's borrowing costs, potentially leading to a "dividend freeze" or reduced capital for GENM's expansion7777.Liquidity Squeeze: The group has already seen delays in other financing, such as the US$561 million bond sale for the Resorts World Catskills hotel, due to the strain of the merger process8888.3. Execution Risk of the NYC ProjectWhile GENM was shortlisted for the New York City (NYC) casino license, this massive project carries its own set of risks:Immense Capital Requirement: Winning the license requires an estimated US$3.3 billion to US$5.5 billion in capital expenditure9999. If Genting struggles to secure this financing under favorable terms, it could further strain the stock price10101010.Licensing Uncertainties: Although shortlisted, the license is still subject to final security and background checks through December 31, 2025111111111111111111. Minority Shareholder DisadvantagesIf GENM remains listed but Genting Berhad holds a dominant stake (currently over 73%), minority shareholders may face:Low Liquidity: As the public spread narrows, it may become harder to buy or sell large blocks of shares without significantly moving the price13131313.Dividend Uncertainty: The group may prioritize debt repayment or NYC capex over paying dividends to minority shareholders in the near term14141414.Summary for Investors: Buying below the takeover price offers a potential entry point for long-term growth (especially the NYC upside), but it exposes you to the high leverage of the parent company and the risk that the stock remains stagnant for a long period while the group manages its debt15151515.

author: StakesAreHigh
body: PETALING JAYA: CIMB Research has upgraded Genting Malaysia Bhd to “buy” from “hold”. The research house also raised its target price for the integrated casino resort operator by 6% to RM2.70. Last month, Genting Malaysia was awarded a full licence for its of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) operations, currently operating as a” racino”, a combined horse racing track or other live betting facility. The company has allocated US$5.5bil to convert the racino into an integrated casino resort, the first phase of which is expected to start operations in the second quarter of this year. CIMB Research said its higher target price factored in the earnings boost from the RWNYC casino operations. This was partly offset by a rollback in the assumption of a US$300mil debt reduction for the company’s Empire Resorts Inc, which owns Resorts World Catskills (RWC), following a delay in the sale of RWC’s non-gaming assets. “We acknowledge that Genting Malaysia’s share price may take some time to re-rate as investors could stay on the sidelines until Genting Malaysia delivers strong core earnings-per-share (EPS) growth in 2027, driven by RWNYC,” the research house said. It also does not expect dividends in the 2025 and 2027 time frame, as the company conserves cash to reduce debt and partly fund RWNYC’s expansion. The shares currently trade at 7.4 times enterprise value over forecast earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation for this year, or a 20% discount to its 10-year pre-Covid 19 mean. The research house has cut this year’s core EPS forecast by 8% to factor in the higher interest cost on debt raised by RWNYC to pay for the upfront licence fee and capital expenditure for the initial phase of expansion, while taking into consideration that new table games (250 out of a total 800) would not be sufficient to offset the impact. “However, we have raised our core EPS estimate for next year by 25% on the full-year impact from table-games operation and an increase to 400 tables by next January. “After the revisions, we expect Genting Malaysia’s core EPS to dip slightly by 1% year-on-year (y-o-y) this year before surging 39% y-o-y in 2027,” the research house added. In the third quarter ended Sept 30 last year (3Q25), Genting Malaysia’s net profit dropped 79% y-o-y to RM119.7mil, mainly due to lower foreign exchange gains. This translated to an earnings per share of 2.11 sen. This was despite higher revenue, which increased by 22% y-o-y to RM3.4bil, contributed by better performance from the leisure and hospitality business in Malaysia, Britain, Egypt, the United States and the Bahamas. In Malaysia, the group’s leisure and hospitality operations recorded a 19% increase in revenue to RM1.99bil, mainly driven by higher overall business volumes in the gaming segment at Resorts World Genting. For the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2025 (9M25), the group’s net profit fell by 14% to RM609mil, or an earnings per share of 10.75 sen. Revenue saw an 8% uptick y-o-y to RM8.9bil in the 9M25, mainly from the leisure and hospitality businesses across all geographical segments due to a higher volume of business.

author: Daim88
body: It is not true that Genting is restricted for only 6 months; under Malaysian takeover rules, an offeror whose bid has lapsed is generally restricted from making another offer or acquiring more than 2% of the target's shares for 12 months from the lapse date unless a waiver is granted. Genting Bhd's recent takeover offer for Genting Malaysia Bhd lapsed on December 1, 2025. Genting Bhd's offer to take Genting Malaysia private officially closed on December 1, 2025, with the company securing a 73.13% stake, which was short of the 75% needed for delisting. Following the lapse of the offer, the following regulatory restrictions apply under Malaysian rules: 12-Month Restriction on New Offer: Genting cannot announce another offer or possible offer for Genting Malaysia within 12 months from the lapse date (December 1, 2025) without the consent of the authorities. 2% Acquisition Cap: During this 12-month period, Genting is also restricted from acquiring more than an additional 2% of Genting Malaysia's shares through open-market purchases. This constraint makes it difficult for Genting to incrementally reach the 75% threshold needed for delisting during this timeframe.

author: Daim88
body: Genting only requires another 1.87% acquisition from the open market; this means Genting won't break any rules if they are to incrementally reach the 75% threshold needed for delisting during this timeframe. Meaning, Genting can trigger take over any time, if they choose to by reaching 75% ownership. Genting seems to have planned this meticulously making sure that they have the upper hand and won't break any rules. They are holding all the cards now.

body: Genting Malaysia’s share price is depressed mainly because its casino operations slipped into losses in early 2026 due to transition costs, weak margins, and investor concerns about slow recovery in the leisure/hospitality sector. Despite Genting Berhad’s group-level profit surge from joint ventures, Genting Malaysia itself is struggling, which explains why investors are cautious. --- 📉 Key Reasons for Weak Share Price - Casino transition costs Genting Malaysia reported losses tied to restructuring and transition expenses in its casino operations, eroding investor confidence. - Low margins Net profit margin is only 3.46%, with return on equity at 0.29%, far below industry peers. - High volatility The stock has swung between RM 2.20 – RM 3.59 in the past year, reflecting uncertainty and lack of strong buying support. - Investor sentiment Analysts note results “below expectations,” with some issuing HOLD calls rather than BUY, signaling limited near-term upside. --- 📊 Current Market Snapshot (May 2026) | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | Share Price | RM 2.35 | | 52-week Range | RM 2.20 – RM 3.59 | | Market Cap | RM 9.1B | | Dividend Yield | ~2.1% | | P/E Ratio | 106.3 (extremely high, showing weak earnings) | | Volume | ~7M shares traded daily | --- ⚠️ Risks & Challenges - High debt load and capital-intensive projects limit flexibility. - Competition from regional casinos (Macau, Singapore) pressures margins. - Tourism recovery uncertainty — slower-than-expected rebound in visitor numbers affects revenue. - Regulatory risks — government policies on gaming licenses and taxes remain unpredictable. ---

author: Good123
body: Executive Summary Maintain BUY with lower TP of MYR2.92 (-11%) Earnings missed our expectations on cost pressures Cut FY26E but raise FY27E and FY28E earnings Future earnings ought to be much stronger Detail Maintain BUY with lower TP of MYR2.92 (-11%) 1Q26 results underwhelmed on payroll cost pressures at RWG, GENUK and RWNYC. We cut FY26E earnings by 11% on lower RWG and GENUK EBITDA margins, but raise FY27E/FY28E earnings by 25%/26% on RWNYC table games contribution. Thus, we trim our SOTP-TP to MYR2.92 from MYR3.27. Earnings should strengthen from 2Q26 onwards, supported by RWNYC table games revenue and lower gaming machine tax rates. We do not discount the possibility that GENT will attempt to takeover GENM again. Earnings missed our expectations on cost pressures 1Q26 core net profit of MYR10.2m accounted for only 1% of our FY estimate. 1Q26 EBITDA of MYR630.5m fared better than core net profit, being a tad below our expectations at 20% of our FY estimate. The shortfall was due to :- (i) 1Q26 RWG EBITDA margin of 31% or 1ppt lower than expected on higher payroll cost; (ii) 1Q26 GENUK EBITDA margin of 11% or 5ppts lower than expected on higher payroll and National Health Service costs; and (iii) higher payroll costs at RWNYC as it ramped up hiring of table dealers before it launched table games on 28 Apr 2026. Cut FY26E but raise FY27E and FY28E earnings We lower RWG EBITDA to 30% from 31% and GENUK EBITDA to 13% from 16% but note that the said higher payroll cost at RWNYC should be matched by table games revenue from 28 Apr 2026. Imputing FY26E/FY27E/FY28E RWNYC average number of tables of 250/400/600 and average revenue of USD5,500/table/day, we estimate that the table games can contribute USD9m/USD75m/USD85m to group earnings. All in, we cut FY26E earnings by 11% but raise FY27E/FY28E earnings by 25%/26% (Fig. 2). Future earnings ought to be much stronger Going into 2Q26, we expect it to be seasonally weaker for RWG post-Chinese New Year but seasonally stronger for GENUK and RWNYC as summer arrives. Moreover, the gaming machine tax rates at RWNYC have been reduced to 56% from 68% when GENM converted them to slot machines from video lottery terminals on 28 Apr 2026 as well. The impact of this is significant as we estimate that this would boost FY26E earnings by USD68m (MYR270m) or c.USD100m (MYR396m) on a full year basis.

body: Genting Malaysia Bhd's indirect subsidiary, Empire Resorts Inc., has scrapped its proposed capital restructuring after fully redeeming its US$300 million (approx. RM1.22 billion) 7.75% senior secured notes due November 1, 2026. The redemption happened on July 2 (US Eastern time), leading all parties to mutually agree not to proceed.

author: Income
body: Empire Resorts (a casino operator in New York owned indirectly by Genting Malaysia) had US$300 million (~RM1.22 billion) in debt — specifically 7.75% senior secured notes that were due to be repaid by November 1, 2026.

author: Income
body: Earlier (in 2025), Empire announced a proposed capital restructuring plan. This is a big financial reorganization, often involving selling assets, raising new money, changing ownership, or refinancing debt. It was likely done because Empire was losing money and people were worried it might struggle to repay the US$300 million when it matured next year.

author: Income
body: The new development: On July 2, 2026, Empire fully redeemed (paid back) the entire US$300 million debt early. Because the problematic debt is now completely gone, there is no longer any need for the complicated restructuring plan. All parties involved agreed to cancel/drop the restructuring.

author: Income
body: Why is this good news? Paying off the debt early removes a major financial headache and refinancing risk. It avoids the downsides of restructuring (e.g., selling assets cheaply, diluting shareholders, or giving up control). It shows Empire/Genting had enough cash or access to funds to clear this debt cleanly. This strengthens Empire’s balance sheet and reduces uncertainty for Genting Malaysia’s investors.

author: Income
body: Instead of doing a messy financial overhaul to survive the debt deadline, Empire simply paid off the debt and moved on. This is a cleaner and stronger outcome than expected.

author: Good123
body: Full ownership would eliminate the holding-company complexity This is perhaps the strongest argument. At present: Genting Berhad → 73% GENM → Resorts World Genting + UK + US + other businesses With full ownership: Genting Berhad → 100% GENM businesses That allows Genting to make capital-allocation decisions across the group much more freely. For example, cash generated by Resorts World Genting could potentially be allocated directly toward: * Resorts World New York * Genting’s US expansion * UK operations * Malaysian property/entertainment expansion * debt reduction * major redevelopment projects rather than having to consider minority shareholders at GENM level.

author: Good123
body: The New York opportunity makes control particularly valuable This is potentially the big strategic reason. Genting’s group strategy includes major US opportunities. Genting’s 2025 takeover announcement itself linked the consolidation of GENM to strengthening the group’s financial position and capital allocation ahead of its potential New York casino investment. And more recently, Genting and GENM shares have responded positively to renewed optimism surrounding the New York expansion prospects.

author: Good123
body: If the US opportunity becomes sufficiently attractive, Genting may conclude that: “Why share the future upside of GENM’s US assets with minority shareholders when we can own 100%?” That is a legitimate strategic rationale for another attempt.

author: Good123
body: The first offer may actually have been a “price discovery” exercise This is an interesting way to look at the 2025 transaction. The original RM2.35 offer valued GENM at about RM13.9 billion based on its ~5.94 billion shares. Reuters reported that this represented approximately: * 9.1× EV/EBITDA * 1.12× book value * 22.9% premium to the six-month average price. But some analysts argued that RM2.35 undervalued GENM. The Star reported that there was caution over the offer precisely because of this valuation concern. So Genting learnt something very valuable: Minority shareholders may not be willing to surrender GENM cheaply. A future offer could therefore be structured at a higher price designed to secure the remaining shares.

author: Good123
body: The big question: What price? This is where it gets interesting. I would not automatically assume another offer would be RM2.35. If GENM continues recovering, a plausible future offer would need to provide a meaningful premium to the prevailing market price.

author: Good123
body: And there is another powerful argument for GENM shareholders Suppose Genting makes another offer at, say, RM2.80–RM3.00. Minority shareholders would have to decide: Take the cash now vs. Remain invested in a potentially stronger GENM That second option becomes increasingly attractive if: * Resorts World Genting visitor numbers continue recovering; * non-gaming revenue improves; * the new attractions perform; * UK operations improve; * New York assets become more valuable; * earnings continue recovering; * dividends remain sustainable. GENM’s 2025 performance already shows a significant improvement from 2024, with net profit rising from RM0.2 billion to RM0.7 billion and EBITDA from RM2.9 billion to RM3.3 billion.

author: Good123
body: Genting’s first privatisation attempt was not necessarily the end of the story. It may have been the first stage of a longer-term consolidation strategy. Genting has already demonstrated that it wants control. It has increased its GENM ownership to 73.13%. And the underlying GENM business is recovering. Therefore, a future re-offer is strategically logical, particularly if GENM’s share price remains below Genting’s assessment of its long-term intrinsic value.

author: Good123
body: Genting Bhd itself must justify the economics. Genting’s 2025 financial snapshot showed: * Revenue RM27.7b * EBITDA RM8.0b * Net profit RM1.0b * Equity RM47.1b So spending several billion ringgit to buy out GENM minorities is a major capital-allocation decision. Genting would need to demonstrate that owning the remaining 26.87% produces a better return than using that capital elsewhere. Bottom line Yes — I think a renewed GENM privatisation attempt is strategically credible. The logic is: 73.13% ownership already achieved → GENM earnings recovering → US/New York opportunity increasing → simpler group structure → 100% cash-flow control → potential re-offer at a higher price. For GENM shareholders, however, the key is the price. A renewed offer around RM2.35 would be much less compelling; a materially higher offer could become a genuine opportunity to crystallise value. And for Genting Bhd shareholders, the ideal outcome would actually be to acquire the remaining GENM shares without overpaying — because the real prize is the long-term cash flow and strategic control, not simply taking GENM private.

body: Now only RM 1.12 compare to Last Year Genting offered price for GenM at RM 2.35. Genting Bhd’s attempt to privatise Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) failed in December 2025 after Genting fell short of the 75% shareholding threshold required to delist the company from Bursa Malaysia Genting loses takeover bid, wins NYC licence. Key Details of the Privatisation Bid • The Offer: Genting Bhd offered RM2.35 per share (valuing the buyout at roughly RM6.74 billion) to acquire the remaining stake it did not own. • The Timeline: • Launched on October 13, 2025, at a 9.8% to 10% premium over GENM’s last traded price of RM2.14. • Turned unconditional on November 3, 2025, after Genting crossed the 50% ownership threshold. • Extended to December 1, 2025, after reaching only 57% and eventually stalling at a 73.88% stake (short of the mandatory 75% needed for delisting). • Opposition: Independent adviser Kenanga Investment Bank urged minority shareholders to reject the offer, pointing out that it undervalued the company. • Concurrent Events: The bid closed on the same day Resorts World New York City won a major downstate commercial casino licence recommendation
